A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, experiments, and main theoretical results. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Appendix A reports original FEMNIST and Shakespeare experiments on data composition, plus an empirical comparison of LP allocations with discrete-search optima. Outcomes appear in Figures 1 and 3 and Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original data-composition experiments and LP-versus-optimum results in Appendix A, Figures 1 and 3, and Table 2.

M1.justification: The PAC contribution model, LP allocation, finite-cover extension, and PWYC payment rule remain unchanged. The new discussion of pooled ERM clarifies its intended role without specifying a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use FEMNIST character classification and Shakespeare next-character prediction, with the same selected agents and five-agent mixture scenario. The finite-hypothesis-class evaluation remains on FEMNIST.

E2.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same comparison between the LP allocation and the optimum obtained by discrete search. No evaluated comparator is added or removed; cited FL methods do not become experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A and Table 1 retain the sample budgets, CNN/LSTM models, SOAP optimizer, learning rate, and epoch counts. Evaluation metrics, agent-specific testing, uniform costs, and the hypothesis-class-size sweep also match.

E4.justification: The data-composition and sample-budget analyses, handwriting examples, and LP approximation-ratio sweep are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions with different random seeds for Appendix A.1 and retain the same dispersion displays in Figures 1 and 3. No uncertainty-estimation procedure or statistical test is added.

E6.justification: The plotted results and empirical findings match. Table 2 retains all seven LP-to-optimum ratios, including 1.67 at hypothesis-class size 5 and 4.20 at size 50.

T1.justification: Appendix B expands v1's brief multiplier assertion into an explicit smooth-performance model, Lagrangian, KKT stationarity derivation, and concavity discussion. This is a localized mathematical addition; the main theorems and proofs in Appendices C–F remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: equilibrium inefficiency, computational hardness, LP approximation, and PWYC strategyproofness and qualified uniqueness. No main contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets pooled ERM as a theoretical benchmark, clarifies that contribution costs remain known, and expands the existing planner-funding caveat. Sections 2.2 and B also strengthen the interpretation of threshold payoffs as representing smooth accuracy–cost preferences.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 adds that reported disagreement probabilities can be estimated locally or on a shared unlabeled validation set, extending v1's finite-vector reporting description. Experimental implementation details and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work survey are retained. The new Section 6 paragraph additionally positions pooled ERM as a standard theoretical benchmark, explicitly connecting this modeling choice to Mohri et al., Li et al., and Blum et al.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory paragraphs, rewrites and renames Appendix B, and expands some footnotes into main-text discussion. The overall section sequence remains intact; citation style and author information are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, adds the ICLR publication header, rearranges the author block, enlarges Figure 1, and shifts some floats, including Table 1. The same four figures and two tables remain, with their substantive visual content preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 usefully clarifies the ERM benchmark, known costs, and planner funding. However, expanded Appendix B does not reconcile continuous KKT reasoning with integer contributions, claims uniqueness under concavity alone, and introduces an erroneous equality where the utility should subtract cost. These clarity gains and weaknesses in the strengthened mathematical justification leave the net quality change uncertain.
